descriptionChirho: The Qal active participle used as a substantive noun denoting a shepherd or pastor — one whose role or occupation is tending flocks — appearing in singular, plural, feminine, construct, and with articles, prepositions (k-/l-/m-), and possessive suffixes, and translated consistently as راعٍ/رُعَاة (Arabic), 목자 (Korean), mchungaji/wachungaji (Swahili), pastor/pastores (Spanish), चरवाहा/चरवाहे (Hindi).

The transitive verbal sense of actively tending, shepherding, or pasturing a flock (or people metaphorically), where the subject is the shepherd acting upon the flock — expressed across all finite conjugations (imperfect, perfect, imperative, infinitive, consecutive forms) and verbal participles, translated as apacentar/pastorear (Spanish), يَرْعَى transitive (Arabic), 치다/목양하다/먹이다 (Korean), -chunga/-lisha transitive (Swahili), चराना (Hindi).

The intransitive sense where the subject (typically livestock or animals) grazes or feeds on pasture, without a human shepherd as agent — distinguished by Spanish pacer/pastar (vs. transitive apacentar), Swahili -kula 'eat' (vs. -chunga 'tend'), Korean 먹다/풀을뜯다 'eat/pluck grass' (vs. 먹이다 'feed someone'), and feminine-plural subjects indicating animals as actors.

A figurative-destructive extension of the grazing sense where 'feeding on' becomes 'devouring' or 'consuming' with harmful effect — marked by Spanish devorar/quebrar, Arabic يَرْعَى with destructive context, Korean 파괴하다 'destroy', and Swahili -ula 'burn/consume' or -kula with destructive overtone, representing a genuine metaphorical shift from pastoral feeding to predatory consumption.
